div.div: Evidence view for framework coverage, governance capabilities, control mappings, datamodel alignment, confidence, and rationale.

div.p: What this shows: Weighted coverage by governance capability.
How to use it: Use this to see why a framework is strong or weak, then review missing datamodels and control mappings below.

search.query: | stats sum(mapping_weight) as possible_weight sum(covered_weight) as covered_weight dc(control_reference) as controls dc(datamodel) as datamodels dc(eval(if(datamodel_observed=1,datamodel,null()))) as observed_datamodels by capability | eval capability_coverage_pct=round((covered_weight/possible_weight)*100,1) | sort - capability_coverage_pct capability | table capability capability_coverage_pct

div.p: What this shows: Whether the datamodels required by the selected framework/capability mappings were observed in the selected data.
Read it as: Missing means the mapping exists but no supporting datamodel evidence was found in the selected search scope and time range.

search.query: | stats dc(datamodel) as datamodels by coverage_state

| stats sum(mapping_weight) as possible_weight sum(covered_weight) as covered_weight dc(control_reference) as mapped_controls values(framework) as frameworks dc(datamodel) as mapped_datamodels values(eval(if(datamodel_observed=1,datamodel,null()))) as covered_datamodels values(eval(if(datamodel_observed=0,datamodel,null()))) as missing_datamodels by capability | eval capability_coverage_pct=round((covered_weight/possible_weight)*100,1) | eval status=case(capability_coverage_pct>=85,"Strong",capability_coverage_pct>=60,"Partial",capability_coverage_pct>0,"Limited",true(),"No observed coverage") | rename capability as Capability capability_coverage_pct as "Capability Coverage %" status as Status frameworks as Frameworks mapped_controls as "Mapped Controls" mapped_datamodels as "Mapped Datamodels" covered_datamodels as "Covered Datamodels" missing_datamodels as "Missing Datamodels" | table Capability "Capability Coverage %" Status Frameworks "Mapped Controls" "Mapped Datamodels" "Covered Datamodels" "Missing Datamodels" | sort - "Capability Coverage %" Capability

panel.title: Framework to Capability to Datamodel Evidence

div.p: What this shows: The full explainability chain from framework/control area to DIG capability, Splunk datamodel, observed evidence, confidence and rationale.
How to use it: Use this table when someone asks how a framework coverage score was produced.

search.query: | eval evidence=if(datamodel_observed=1,"Observed","Not observed") | eval matched_fields=coalesce(matched_fields,0) | rename framework as Framework framework_version as Version control_reference as Control requirement_area as "Requirement Area" capability as Capability datamodel as Datamodel evidence as Evidence mapping_confidence as Confidence mapping_rationale as Rationale source_terms as "Source Terms" source_url as Source notes as Notes matched_fields as "Matched Fields" | table Framework Version Control "Requirement Area" Capability Datamodel Evidence Confidence "Matched Fields" Rationale "Source Terms" Source Notes | sort Framework Control Capability Datamodel

div.p: What this shows: Which governance frameworks are represented by the selected telemetry based on the configured capability and datamodel mappings.
How to use it: Use this to identify which frameworks are most frequently touched by the selected Data Source population.
Read it as: Higher bars indicate broader telemetry overlap with that governance driver. This is mapping evidence, not a compliance assertion.

search.query: | where governance_mapped=1 | stats dc(group_value) as source_values dc(datamodel) as datamodels dc(field_name) as matched_fields dc(capability) as capabilities by framework | sort - source_values - matched_fields framework

chart.option: Number of Data Source values impacted

panel.title: Mapped vs Unmapped Datamodels by Data Source

div.p: What this shows: The split between datamodels that have governance mapping guidance configured and datamodels that currently do not.
How to use it: Use this to separate mapped governance evidence from areas where the knowledge base or customer-specific policy input may need expansion.
Read it as: Unmapped does not mean unimportant. It means DIG detected datamodel relevance but no governance framework mapping currently exists for that datamodel.

search.query: | stats dc(datamodel) as datamodels by group_value governance_mapped | eval mapping_state=if(governance_mapped=1,"Governance mapped","Unmapped") | rename group_value as "Data Source" | chart sum(datamodels) over "Data Source" by mapping_state

div.p: What this shows: A plain-language summary of governance mapping coverage for each selected Data Source.
How to use it: Use this as the first explanation when discussing governance evidence with admins, consultants, or stakeholders.

search.query: | stats dc(field_name) as matched_dm_fields dc(datamodel) as matched_datamodel_count dc(eval(if(governance_mapped=1,datamodel,null()))) as mapped_datamodel_count dc(eval(if(governance_mapped=0,datamodel,null()))) as unmapped_datamodel_count values(framework) as frameworks values(capability) as capabilities by group_value | eval mapping_coverage_pct=if(matched_datamodel_count>0,round((mapped_datamodel_count/matched_datamodel_count)*100,2),0) | eval brief=case( mapped_datamodel_count=0, "CIM/datamodel relevance was detected, but no governance framework mapping is currently configured for the matched datamodels. Treat this as a governance mapping opportunity rather than a compliance gap.", mapping_coverage_pct>=80, "Most detected datamodel relevance has governance framework mapping configured. This is a strong starting point for framework coverage, retention, tiering and policy alignment conversations.", mapping_coverage_pct>=40, "Some detected datamodel relevance has governance framework mapping configured. Recommendations are useful, but unmapped areas should be reviewed before final decisions are made.", true(), "Limited governance framework mapping is configured for the detected datamodel relevance. Use the evidence below to prioritise mapping expansion and customer policy discussion." ) | eval frameworks=if(isnull(frameworks),"Unmapped",frameworks) | eval capabilities=if(isnull(capabilities),"Unmapped",capabilities) | rename group_value as "Data Source" | table "Data Source" matched_datamodel_count mapped_datamodel_count unmapped_datamodel_count mapping_coverage_pct frameworks capabilities brief | sort - mapping_coverage_pct "Data Source"

div.p: What this shows: Data Source-level governance evidence, mapped frameworks, mapped capabilities, matched datamodels, retention guidance and tiering guidance.
How to use it: Use this to compare Data Source values and identify where guidance exists, where mapping is missing, and where further validation is needed.
Read it as: This is not a compliance assertion. It is an evidence-based view of configured governance mapping and detected datamodel relevance.

search.query: | stats dc(field_name) as matched_dm_fields dc(datamodel) as matched_datamodel_count values(framework) as frameworks values(capability) as capabilities values(datamodel) as datamodels values(eval(if(governance_mapped=1,datamodel,null()))) as governance_mapped_datamodels values(eval(if(governance_mapped=0,datamodel,null()))) as unmapped_datamodels values(governance_relevance) as relevance_values values(retention_importance) as retention_values values(tiering_recommendation) as tiering_values values(searchable_retention_recommendation) as searchable_values values(edge_processing_recommendation) as edge_values max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval frameworks=if(isnull(frameworks),"Unmapped",frameworks) | eval capabilities=if(isnull(capabilities),"Unmapped",capabilities) | eval high_relevance=if(mvfind(relevance_values,"High")>=0,1,0) | eval medhigh_relevance=if(mvfind(relevance_values,"Medium-High")>=0,1,0) | eval medium_relevance=if(mvfind(relevance_values,"Medium")>=0,1,0) | eval governance_relevance=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped", high_relevance=1, "High", medhigh_relevance=1, "Medium-High", medium_relevance=1, "Medium", true(), "Low" ) | eval recommended_tier=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped / review", mvfind(tiering_values,"Tier 1")>=0, "Tier 1", mvfind(tiering_values,"Tier 2")>=0, "Tier 2", mvfind(tiering_values,"Tier 3")>=0, "Tier 3", true(), "Review" ) | eval searchable_retention=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped / review", mvfind(retention_values,"High")>=0, "High", mvfind(retention_values,"Medium-High")>=0, "Medium-High", mvfind(retention_values,"Medium")>=0, "Medium", mvfind(retention_values,"Low")>=0, "Low", true(), "Review" ) | eval edge_processing_guidance=case( governance_mapped=0, "Unmapped / review", isnotnull(edge_values), edge_values, true(), "Review" ) | eval consultant_talking_point=case( governance_relevance="High", "Lead with operational importance: this data appears highly relevant to security, audit or investigation outcomes. Validate ownership, use cases and retention policy.", governance_relevance="Medium-High", "Position as a strong candidate for governance review: evidence exists, but confirm business use and retention expectations.", governance_relevance="Medium", "Use as a prioritisation discussion: decide whether this data supports enough use cases to justify searchable retention or optimisation effort.", governance_relevance="Unmapped", "Frame as a knowledge-base opportunity: DIG found datamodel relevance, but governance framework mapping needs to be configured or validated.", true(), "Use as a review candidate: current evidence suggests limited governance relevance, but confirm against customer policy and business context." ) | rename group_value as "Data Source" | table "Data Source" governance_relevance frameworks capabilities governance_mapped_datamodels unmapped_datamodels matched_dm_fields recommended_tier searchable_retention edge_processing_guidance consultant_talking_point | sort governance_relevance - matched_dm_fields "Data Source"

div.p: What this shows: The datamodel-level evidence behind the recommendation, including mapped frameworks, capabilities and matched field counts.
How to use it: Use this when a customer asks why a Data Source appears governance relevant.
Read it as: Matched fields indicate evidence of datamodel relevance; governance mapping indicates whether DIG has framework/capability guidance configured for that datamodel.

search.query: | stats dc(field_name) as matched_fields values(framework) as frameworks values(control_reference) as controls values(requirement_area) as requirement_areas values(capability) as capabilities values(governance_relevance) as governance_relevance values(mapping_confidence) as mapping_confidence values(retention_importance) as retention_importance values(tiering_recommendation) as tiering_recommendation values(searchable_retention_recommendation) as searchable_retention_recommendation values(edge_processing_recommendation) as edge_processing_recommendation values(notes) as notes max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value datamodel | eval mapping_state=if(governance_mapped=1,"Mapped","Unmapped") | eval frameworks=if(isnull(frameworks),"Unmapped",frameworks) | eval capabilities=if(isnull(capabilities),"Unmapped",capabilities) | rename group_value as "Data Source" datamodel as Datamodel | table "Data Source" Datamodel mapping_state frameworks controls requirement_areas capabilities matched_fields governance_relevance mapping_confidence retention_importance tiering_recommendation searchable_retention_recommendation edge_processing_recommendation notes | sort "Data Source" mapping_state - matched_fields Datamodel

| where datamodel_observed=1 | mvexpand matched_field_names | rename matched_field_names as field_name groups as "Data Source values" framework as Framework capability as Capability datamodel as Datamodel | stats values(Framework) as Frameworks values(Capability) as Capabilities values(Datamodel) as Datamodels values("Data Source values") as "Data Source values" by field_name | eval source_type_count=mvcount('Data Source values') | rename field_name as Field source_type_count as "Data Source Count" | table Field "Data Source Count" Datamodels Capabilities Frameworks "Data Source values" | sort - "Data Source Count" Field | head 250
